short: MYB factors bind the Myb binding site (MBS), a six-base element written YAACKG, through two or three imperfect ~52-residue repeats that each fold into a helix-turn-helix-like unit. Humans have three true MYB proteins: MYB (c-Myb), MYBL1 (A-Myb) and MYBL2 (B-Myb). Only repeats R2 and R3 are required for sequence-specific binding, and their recognition helices sit side by side in one major groove. MYB proteins control hematopoietic progenitor expansion, spermatogenesis and, for MYBL2, mitotic gene expression through the MuvB complex. MYB is duplicated in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia and fused to NFIB in adenoid cystic carcinoma. This family key also collects Myb/SANT-fold archetypes whose proteins are not MYB factors and do not bind the MBS, which is the main source of confusion here.
long:
## The factors

Three human genes encode true MYB transcription factors: MYB (c-Myb), MYBL1 (A-Myb) and MYBL2
(B-Myb); HOCOMOCO labels them MYB, MYBA and MYBB, and the Vierstra archetypes use the group
name MYBL. Their DNA-binding domain is built from three imperfect repeats of about 52 residues,
R1, R2 and R3, each containing three regularly spaced tryptophans and folding into a
helix-turn-helix-related unit. R1 is dispensable: R2 and R3 alone give specific binding, which is
why plant and fungal homologues are usually R2R3 proteins. MYB is expressed in immature
hematopoietic cells, colonic crypt epithelium and some neural progenitors; MYBL1 is highest in
testis and germinal-center B cells; MYBL2 is a cell-cycle gene, rising in S phase and peaking at
G2/M. This atlas key is deliberately broader than the three MYB proteins, because the Myb/SANT
fold is reused by proteins that are not MYB factors. In the current data those extras are DMTF1
(DMP1, a cyclin D-binding Myb-like protein), MYPOP (a Myb-related protein that partners profilin)
and TTF1 (the RNA polymerase I transcription termination factor, not the thyroid factor NKX2-1,
which is unfortunately also called TTF-1). TERF1 and TERF2, whose telobox is a Myb-like repeat,
are held in a separate TELOBOX family here; SNAPC4, which uses Myb repeats to bind the snRNA
proximal sequence element, has no motif in these databases. The SANT domain itself, found in
chromatin remodelers and corepressors, has the Myb fold but is thought to read histone tails
rather than DNA sequence.

## The motif

The literature consensus for the MBS is YAACKG, six bases, usually quoted as PyAAC(G/T)G. The
invariant part is AAC followed by G or T then G; the identity comes from the recognition helix of
R3 inserting into the major groove with R2 packed alongside, so the two repeats read one
continuous site and the cavity in R2 rearranges on binding. Database renderings differ mainly by
strand and by doubling. JASPAR MYB (MA0100.4) and the corresponding CIS-BP model give CAACTG,
which is YAACKG with Y=C and K=T; the HOCOMOCO ChIP model GGCAGTTG is the same site read on the
other strand. The data consensus for the family as a whole, CCGTTA, is the reverse complement of
TAACGG, again the same core. In vitro selection on MYBL1 and MYBL2 returns longer, near-palindromic
models such as AACCGTTAACGG and CCGTTAAACSG: these are two MBS half-sites in inverted orientation
and reflect how the isolated domains bind selected DNA, not a different specificity. Within the
three MYB proteins nothing is separable by sequence. The non-MYB members are separable, and they
are not MBS models: DMTF1's high-quality integrative model is CCCGGATG, MYPOP's is GCGCAA, and
TTF1's is the rDNA Sal box terminator, recognizable by its internal GACCAG. Their nearest
neighbours across the four databases fall outside this family, and the family's cohesion (0.72
over 22 motifs) is lower than for a single-specificity family for exactly that reason.

## Where it acts

MYB sites are short and occur in both promoters and enhancers. In hematopoietic cells c-Myb
occupies thousands of sites and cooperates with CEBP factors, RUNX1, GATA2 and the coactivators
CBP/p300; classic targets include MYC, KIT, CCNB1 and, in T cells, TCR genes. MYBL2 behaves
differently: it is recruited to mitotic promoters mainly as a subunit of the MYB-MuvB (MMB)
complex, which hands over from the repressive DREAM complex at G1/S, and MuvB's own sequence
anchor is the CHR element read by LIN54, not the MBS. Consequently much of the MYBL2 signal in
chromatin immunoprecipitation sits on CHR-containing promoters where the underlying sequence is
not a Myb site at all. TTF1 sites are confined to the rDNA repeat, where the Sal box terminates
Pol I transcription, so its motif is genomically almost absent outside the rDNA and its
nucleolar-organizer copies.

## Biology and disease

Mice lacking c-Myb die around embryonic day 15 with a failure of fetal hepatic hematopoiesis, the
sharpest demonstration that MYB is needed for progenitor expansion rather than for lineage
identity. Mybl1-null male mice are sterile with a meiotic arrest, and Mybl2 loss is lethal at the
blastocyst stage. In cancer, MYB is more often amplified, translocated or driven by a new enhancer
than mutated: tandem duplication of MYB occurs in T-cell acute lymphoblastic leukemia, and a
recurrent MYB-NFIB fusion defines most adenoid cystic carcinomas of salivary gland and breast.
MYBL2 overexpression is a component of proliferation signatures in many tumors and is largely a
readout of cell-cycle activity.

## Reading a hit

A YAACKG match is six informative bases and will occur by chance roughly every few hundred base
pairs on either strand, so a single hit is close to meaningless without other evidence. The three
MYB proteins cannot be separated from sequence, so a hit means "a MYB-family site" at best, and
expression context is what narrows it: MYB in immature hematopoietic cells, MYBL1 in testis and
germinal centers, MYBL2 in cycling cells. The bigger hazard in this key is the label. Several
members are Myb/SANT-fold proteins that do not bind the MBS, and a match scored against the
DMTF1, MYPOP or TTF1 models is a match to an unrelated sequence that happens to share the family
key. For MYBL2, treat ChIP-derived enrichment with care: recruitment through MuvB to CHR
elements means a B-Myb peak often marks a LIN54 site rather than a Myb site.
caveats: Two problems compound here. First, the MBS is six bases, so chance matches are abundant and the three MYB paralogues are indistinguishable by sequence. Second, this key is a fold class, not a single specificity: DMTF1 (CCCGGATG), MYPOP (GCGCAA) and TTF1 (the rDNA Sal box) are Myb/SANT-fold proteins whose motifs are unrelated to the MBS, and the CIS-BP MYPOP model is transferred from mouse. The family cohesion of 0.72 reflects this mixture. For MYBL2, ChIP-derived signal is frequently recruitment through the MuvB complex onto LIN54's CHR element rather than direct MBS binding, so a B-Myb peak is not evidence of a Myb site.
